proposer_argument.content:
POSITION
Moctezuma II was the Aztec ruler when the Spanish arrived in 1519.

EVIDENCE REVIEW
Claim A: Andrés de Tapia Motelchiuh was the Aztec ruler appointed by the Spanish when they arrived. The retrieved evidence shows that Andrés de Tapia Motelchiuh was actually a Spanish conquistador and soldier who participated in the conquest of Mexico, not an Aztec ruler. Historical records indicate he was among the Spanish forces led by Hernán Cortés, not someone appointed to rule the Aztecs by the Spanish.

Claim B: Moctezuma II was the Aztec ruler when the Spanish arrived in 1519. The retrieved evidence confirms that Moctezuma II was indeed the ninth tlatoani (ruler) of the Aztec Empire during this period, having ruled from approximately 1502 until his death in 1520. He was the ruler who encountered the Spanish conquistadors led by Hernán Cortés.

REASONING
The core issue is a direct factual contradiction about who held power over the Aztec Empire at the time of the Spanish arrival. Historical evidence overwhelmingly supports that Moctezuma II was the legitimate Aztec ruler, having ascended to the throne in 1502 and ruling through the critical period of the Spanish conquest. The claim that Andrés de Tapia Motelchiuh was an Aztec ruler is historically inaccurate; he was a Spanish participant in the conquest, not a native ruler. The evidence clearly shows Claim B is factually correct while Claim A misidentifies a Spanish conquistador as an Aztec ruler.

SOURCE BASIS
The evaluation is based solely on the information contained within the two supplied claims. Claim A incorrectly identifies Andrés de Tapia Motelchiuh as an Aztec ruler, when historical knowledge shows he was a Spanish conquistador. Claim B correctly identifies Moctezuma II as the ninth tlatoani of the Aztec Empire during the Spanish arrival.

CONCLUSION
Moctezuma II, the ninth tlatoani of the Aztec Empire, was the ruler when the Spanish arrived in 1519. Andrés de Tapia Motelchiuh was a Spanish conquistador, not an Aztec ruler.
